vulnerability_patterns.description: An off-by-one bounds check allowed trace.rx_trace_pos[i] == RDS_MSG_RX_DGRAM_TRACE_MAX to pass validation. That boundary value is outside the valid index range for arrays sized RDS_MSG_RX_DGRAM_TRACE_MAX, and later trace consumers may use the stored value as or to derive an array index.
trigger_conditions: rds_recv_track_latency iterates 'for (i = 0; i < rs->rs_rx_traces; i++)' and validates each trace.rx_trace_pos[i]
trace.rx_trace_pos[i] equal to RDS_MSG_RX_DGRAM_TRACE_MAX is accepted instead of causing 'rs->rs_rx_traces = 0; return -EFAULT;'
the accepted value can propagate into receive trace state and be consumed as an index or index-derived value by later receive-message trace handling
fix_patterns: on boundary violation, reset 'rs->rs_rx_traces = 0' and return '-EFAULT'

suggestions: First-draft detector should anchor on the patch-local guard shape: 'if (value > MAX)' guarding a value that is later accepted as an index-like position, where valid values are expected to be '< MAX'.
Use 'trace.rx_trace_pos[i]' and 'RDS_MSG_RX_DGRAM_TRACE_MAX' as the minimal patch-local anchors; the important semantic delta is rejecting equality with the max constant.

Do not make the newly added '>=' guard a hard negative filter in the first draft; instead, report pre-fix strict '>' checks against array-size or max-count constants when the value can be stored or propagated.
Treat the reset-and-return path 'rs->rs_rx_traces = 0; return -EFAULT;' as the barrier that should execute for both greater-than and equal-to-max values.

A local AST/CFG check is enough to find the changed validation bug in rds_recv_track_latency; data-flow tracking is useful only to connect the accepted trace position to later index consumers such as rds_cmsg_recv.

Cross-file analysis is not required for a first patch-local checker, although a second-stage refinement may follow trace.rx_trace_pos[i] into rs->rs_rx_trace[i] and then into receive trace array indexing.

analysis_rationale: The patch changes a single bounds guard in net/rds/af_rds.c:rds_recv_track_latency from '>' to '>=' for trace.rx_trace_pos[i] against RDS_MSG_RX_DGRAM_TRACE_MAX. Before the patch, a value equal to RDS_MSG_RX_DGRAM_TRACE_MAX was accepted and stored through the receive-trace state, enabling a later consumer to use an invalid trace index. The commit text explicitly ties this accepted boundary value to an out-of-bounds read in rds_cmsg_recv via inc->i_rx_lat_trace[j + 1].
